newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin names agriculture minister new deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin names agriculture minister new deputy PM.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin named on Monday Agriculture Minister Viktor Khlystun Russia's new deputy prime minister, the presidential press office said.
"The president signed a decree appointing Khlystun to the new post," a Kremlin spokesman said. "He will also retain his current ministerial post."

Khlystun becomes the seventh deputy prime minister in a new-look cabinet which was first dramatically reshuffled in March. The government also has two first deputy prime ministers who are senior to the seven.
The appointment of Khlystun, who has said he is committed to reforming Russia's vast, costly and beleagured farm sector, returns to the agriculture lobby a senior cabinet voice.
The March reshuffle swept away Alexander Zaveryukha, a conservative deputy prime minister who presided over the worst harvests in three decades.
Khlystun is seeking to raise money for the farm sector through commercial banks and he wants to rely less on government handouts, subsidies and barter operations.
